lesson_title: What One Samoosa Costs: Manufacturing and Cost Calculations
hook_text: She sold 500 samoosas at R5 each and lost money on every single one. Here's the number she never checked.
clip_script: Mrs Pillay takes an order: five hundred samoosas for a family function. Pastry and filling — R2,50 each. The helper who folds and fries — R1,50 each. That's R4 inside every samoosa: two thousand rand of prime cost. Then the quiet costs: gas R450, pot wear R50, the cousin watching the frying R250 — R750 of overheads, the cost of keeping the kitchen cooking. Total: R2 750. Divide by five hundred — R5,50. THAT is what one samoosa costs. Sell at R8 and each one clears R2,50 — the order banks R1 250. But price at R5 because a rival did, and every single samoosa sells at a fifty-cent loss that FEELS like business while it quietly eats her savings. The unit cost is the floor under the price. A maker who doesn't know it isn't pricing — only guessing. Same maths runs a stool workshop, a bakery, a factory: sort the costs, stack the layers, divide. Then name your price with your eyes open.
visual_style: Kitchen-counter build: samoosa layers stacking as cost layers (pastry, hands, gas flame), a running total climbing to R5,50, then two price tags — R8 glowing green, R5 cracking red with coins leaking away.
mood: Streetwise and eye-opening — the hidden number under every price.
pacing: Quick layer-by-layer build, hard stop on the R5,50 reveal, punchy close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the floor under your price.
